name: Gediz Vallis Ridge
description: Steep debris channel on the flank of Mount Sharp where Curiosity discovered pure elemental sulfur stones in 2024 before ascending toward the boxwork unit.

mission.name: Curiosity Rover (MSL)
mission.note: Crushed a rock in Gediz Vallis channel revealing pure yellow sulfur crystals never before seen on Mars.

name: Mount Sharp Boxwork Formations
description: Extensive web-like polygonal mineral ridges on Mount Sharp formed when ancient mineral-rich groundwater percolated through bedrock fractures and cemented them against wind erosion.

mission.name: Curiosity Rover (MSL)
mission.note: Investigated the cemented polygonal fracture ridges on Mount Sharp to test whether subsurface fluids sustained habitable niches as Mars dried out.

name: Bradbury Landing (Gale)
description: Touchdown site of NASA's Curiosity rover on Aeolis Palus inside northern Gale Crater, serving as the primary base camp for Mount Sharp surface traverses.

mission.name: Curiosity Rover (MSL)
mission.note: Measured baseline surface radiation (0.64 mSv/sol) with RAD and discovered ancient stream cobbles.

name: Yellowknife Bay
description: Fine-grained Sheepbed mudstone embayment where Curiosity drilled its first sample and proved Gale Crater once held a calm, fresh-water lake suitable for chemolithoautotrophic microbes.

mission.name: Curiosity Rover (MSL)
mission.note: CheMin and SAM identified smectite clays, sulfur, nitrogen, hydrogen, oxygen, phosphorus, and carbon.

name: Mount Sharp Sulfate Unit
description: Upper sulfate-bearing strata of Mount Sharp recording the planetary transition from ancient wet clay-forming lakes to a colder, more arid Martian climate.

mission.name: MRO CRISM & Curiosity
mission.note: Orbital CRISM spectra and surface CheMin mineralogy confirm magnesium and calcium sulfate salts.

name: Octavia E. Butler Landing
description: Touchdown site of the Perseverance rover and Ingenuity helicopter on the crater floor of Jezero, adjacent to the fractured Máaz and Séítah igneous units.

mission.name: Perseverance Rover
mission.note: Cached titanium sample tubes at Three Forks depot and demonstrated MOXIE oxygen production.

name: Jezero Delta Front
description: Steeply layered sedimentary fan deposited where an ancient river emptied into Lake Jezero over 3.5 billion years ago—one of the highest-priority astrobiology sites on Mars.

mission.name: Perseverance Rover
mission.note: Collected mudstone and carbonate cores containing organic molecules and 'leopard spot' redox textures.

name: Neretva Vallis Inlet
description: The western inflow channel that breached the Jezero Crater rim and supplied water and mineral sediment to the ancient crater lake.

mission.name: Perseverance Rover
mission.note: Sampled the 'Cheyava Falls' rock in Neretva Vallis before climbing the western crater rim.

name: Jezero Crater
description: A 45 km diameter impact basin on the western edge of Isidis Planitia that once held a standing lake with both inlet and outlet river valleys.

mission.name: Mars 2020 Perseverance
mission.note: Primary target for the NASA-ESA Mars Sample Return campaign.

name: Nili Fossae
description: Concentric graben troughs northwest of Jezero exposing some of the largest phyllosilicate clay, olivine, and carbonate deposits on Mars.

mission.name: Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter
mission.note: CRISM hyperspectral mapping identified abundant iron-magnesium clays and carbonate outcrops.

name: Isidis Planitia
description: Giant smooth impact basin east of Jezero Crater offering flat lowland terrain and high atmospheric pressure for landing systems.

mission.name: MGS MOLA & MRO
mission.note: Mapped by MOLA laser altimetry and SHARAD subsurface radar.

name: Syrtis Major
description: Low-relief Hesperian shield volcano southwest of Jezero covered in dark basaltic sand sheets and silica-rich volcanic cones.

mission.name: Mars Global Surveyor & Odyssey
mission.note: TES and THEMIS mapped dust-free basaltic bedrock and dacite domes.

name: Tyrrhena Terra
description: Heavily cratered Noachian highlands south of Isidis featuring ancient valley networks and impact megabreccia.

mission.name: Mars Express & MRO
mission.note: HRSC and CTX imaged dendritic drainage channels carved by early Martian precipitation.

name: Olympus Mons
description: The tallest planetary shield volcano in the solar system, rising nearly 22 km above the Martian datum with a 6 km basal cliff escarpment.

mission.name: Mars Global Surveyor (MOLA)
mission.note: Laser altimetry profiled the 80 km summit caldera complex and aureole landslide lobes.

name: Valles Marineris
description: A 4,000 km tectonic canyon system reaching 7 km deep, exposing kilometers of layered volcanic and sedimentary crust.

mission.name: Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter
mission.note: HiRISE and CRISM revealed recurring slope lineae and thick interior layered sulfate mounds.
